smoking_behavior.quit_intention: Will quit in the next month

rated_messages.input_message: Imagine your 'you' from next year has come to visit, and guess what? You quit! How good is that?
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
Try chewing gum if you have trouble resisting smoking when other people light up around you.
Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
Urges can feel like stormy weather. But if you're the sky, you just let that storm come and go on it's own knowing that it won't last forever.

Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.

When running a marathon, the hardest part is often towards the end, but many runners stick with it, knowing that the pain will pass. Learning to quit smoking is like running a marathon - if it gets hard, you may be closer to succeeding than you realize!
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
Acknowledge your unhelpful thought by writing it down on a piece of paper. Then let it be on it's way by crumpling it up and tossing it in a trash can.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
